contracts.text: `|>` must tokenize as a distinct token type — not as bitwise `|` followed by `>`.
A pipe query begins with a standalone `FROM` clause at base indentation (i.e., the `FROM` keyword is not preceded by `SELECT` or any other clause on the same line).
Each subsequent `|>` step occupies its own line at base indentation.
The pipe operator `|>` and the clause keyword that follows it share the same line.
The body of an indented pipe clause (`WHERE`, `SELECT`, `ORDER BY`, `AGGREGATE`, `EXTEND`, `SET`, `DROP`) starts on the next line, indented one level deeper than the `|>` line.
The body of a one-line pipe clause (`LIMIT`, `JOIN` and its variants, `AS`) stays on the same line as the `|>` and keyword.
An `AGGREGATE` pipe clause with a nested `GROUP BY` sub-clause places `GROUP BY` on its own indented line and its body on a further indented line, forming its own indentation level.
contracts.adverse_condition: The `AGGREGATE` clause contains a `GROUP BY` sub-clause. When `GROUP BY` is absent, this nested-indentation requirement does not apply.

contracts.text: Each `|>` operator resets indentation to base level for the next pipe step.
A semicolon attaches after the final pipe step (not after every pipe step and not on a separate line).
Pipe queries nested inside parentheses as subqueries are formatted correctly with the pipe structure preserved within the parentheses.
Traditional (non-pipe) BigQuery query formatting remains unchanged when pipe support is added.
The `keywordCase` setting governs the casing of all pipe keywords including pipe-exclusive ones (`AGGREGATE`, `EXTEND`, `SET`, `DROP`, `AS`).
Pipe clauses produce structured parse nodes; `AGGREGATE` and `EXTEND` are promoted to reserved clauses when they appear after `|>`.
contracts.adverse_condition: The keyword `AGGREGATE` or `EXTEND` appears immediately after `|>` (not in a traditional query context).

contracts.text: `GROUP BY` within an `AGGREGATE` pipe clause nests as a sub-clause parse node with its own indentation level.
contracts.adverse_condition: `GROUP BY` appears inside an `AGGREGATE` pipe clause.

contracts.text: Mixed pipe and traditional statements in the same input format independently (each statement follows its own formatting rules without interference from the other style).
contracts.adverse_condition: The input contains both a pipe-style statement and a traditional-style statement.

contracts.text: The indentation pattern for the body of each clause type in a pipe query matches the indentation pattern the formatter already uses for that same clause type in traditional queries.
All work is on a new branch created from `main`.
All work is committed when done.

Pipe-exclusive clauses are recognized: `AGGREGATE` (with optional nested `GROUP BY`), `EXTEND` (for computed columns), `SET` (for replacing values), `DROP` (for removing columns), and `AS` (for naming intermediates).
